message.content: {"authoring_prompt":"List the specific host-enforced controls required so servers cannot read the whole conversation or see into other servers. Include: keeping the full conversation history local; providing only the minimal contextual information each server needs; maintaining isolated per-server connections; and mediating or blocking cross-server interactions. For each control briefly state how the host enforces it. Conclude with the security implications if any control is violated (how servers could read the entire conversation or access other servers' data, breaking isolation and exposing sensitive context).","suggested_opener":"Your host accidentally transmits full conversation history to a per-server connection.","quiz_type_used":"APPLICATION"}

{"authoring_prompt":"Explain why all MCP implementations MUST support the Base Protocol and Lifecycle Management. Analyze how core JSON-RPC message types, connection initialization, capability negotiation, and session control form the minimal interoperable core. Describe the architectural implications for server and client design, including required lifecycle behaviors and a modular separation-of-concerns that allows optional components to be added or omitted. Give one concrete example of a mandatory behavior and one example of integrating an optional component cleanly.","suggested_opener":"During design review, a colleague questions requiring JSON-RPC and lifecycle management.","quiz_type_used":"ANALYSIS"}

{"authoring_prompt":"Give the candidate one or more MCP/JSON-RPC response examples and ask them to evaluate compliance. Require verification that each response includes the same ID as its request and sets exactly one of `result` or `error`. If the response uses `error`, require the error object to include an integer `code` and a `message`. Have the candidate enumerate which failure mode(s) are present (both set, none set, non-integer code, mismatched/unknown ID) and describe minimal corrective changes.","suggested_opener":"A production incident occurs when MCP/JSON-RPC responses include non-integer error codes.","quiz_type_used":"APPLICATION"}

{"authoring_prompt":"Ask the candidate to design an implementation for an MCP receiver that uses STDIO transport and may lack an authorization context. Describe how credentials and access control become host-local concerns and when the receiver must bind tasks to an authorization context. Specify concrete safeguards: generate cryptographically secure task IDs with sufficient entropy, use shorter TTLs when context-binding is unavailable, reject tasks/get, tasks/result, and tasks/cancel requests across contexts, and ensure tasks/list returns only the requestor\u0019s tasks. Include rate limiting and documentation practices to mitigate enumeration and DoS risks.","suggested_opener":"A production service uses STDIO transport and provides no authorization context.","quiz_type_used":"IMPLEMENTATION"}

{"authoring_prompt":"Produce an implementation plan to harden a server+client pipeline that integrates heterogeneous tools. Enumerate concrete server-side measures: validate all tool inputs, implement proper access controls, rate limit tool invocations, sanitize tool outputs, and publish/enforce input/output schemas. Enumerate concrete client-side measures: prompt for user confirmation on sensitive operations, show tool inputs before calls, validate tool results before passing to the LLM, enforce timeouts, and log tool usage. Provide brief API-contract examples, error-handling flows that surface tool execution errors, and one checklist to prevent data exfiltration.","suggested_opener":"During a code review, you find unchecked Google Calendar API inputs and annotations.","quiz_type_used":"IMPLEMENTATION"}

{"authoring_prompt":"Decide whether to use registry-listed public MCP servers or a custom/self-hosted MCP for a production service. State your choice and justify it by explicitly referencing control tradeoffs: authentication, access control, data handling, tooling, and SLAs. List the responsibilities self-hosting shifts to the integrator: designing/operating (scaling, monitoring, backup), capability discovery and schema/version compatibility, enforcing authz and tenant isolation, sandboxing/vetting tools and resources, and compliance and upgrade procedures. For each responsibility, briefly describe how you would satisfy it while preserving SLAs.","suggested_opener":"Your team must evaluate authentication, access control, SLAs for registry or self-hosted MCP.","quiz_type_used":"APPLICATION"}

{"authoring_prompt":"Explain how an MCP server must implement receiving JSON-RPC batches. Describe parsing an incoming JSON array that contains multiple requests and/or notifications, and how the server should accept and process array-encoded batches even if it never sends batches itself. Call out required behaviors (MUST support receiving) versus optional behaviors (MAY support sending), and enumerate error-handling and validation decisions for malformed arrays or mixed request/notification entries.","suggested_opener":"During a code review you find MCP implementations ignoring array-encoded JSON-RPC batches.","quiz_type_used":"IMPLEMENTATION"}

{"authoring_prompt":"Analyze architectural implications of servers expressing intent using abstract modelPreferences (priority values and optional hints). Explain how clients must interpret priorities and map hints — treated as flexible substrings evaluated in order — to models they actually have access to, and how they may map hints to equivalent models from other providers. Discuss design choices for enforcing that clients retain control over actual model access, selection, and permissions, given that hints are advisory and clients make the final model selection. Identify key failure modes and mitigation strategies.","suggested_opener":"During design, servers send abstract modelPreferences; clients map hints to providers.","quiz_type_used":"ANALYSIS"}

{"authoring_prompt":"Implement server-side handling for tasks/get, tasks/result, and tasks/cancel per the quoted protocol. Return standard JSON-RPC error -32602 for invalid or nonexistent taskId in those endpoints. Reject tasks/cancel requests for terminal-status tasks (completed, failed, cancelled) with error -32602. For valid cancellation, attempt to stop execution and transition the task to cancelled before responding; ensure cancelled remains even if execution later completes or fails. Describe how your implementation handles deletion and ttl-based purging of cancelled or expired tasks.","suggested_opener":"An API gateway issues tasks/cancel for a taskId already marked completed.","quiz_type_used":"IMPLEMENTATION"}

{"authoring_prompt":"Describe realistic interoperability failures that occur when SDKs or spec versions diverge in functionality or protocol features. Explain how ensuring all SDKs provide the same core functionality and full protocol support, and building MCP clients that can connect to any MCP server, prevents and recovers from those failures. Give concrete examples of cross-SDK mismatches and show how alignment of implementations reduces them.","suggested_opener":"During a production incident, MCP clients fail due to SDK protocol mismatches.","quiz_type_used":"APPLICATION"}

{"authoring_prompt":"You have a server exposing the Tools API but client discovery and notifications are failing. Ask the candidate to (a) explain why a server MUST declare the tools capability in its capabilities document, (b) provide the exact JSON snippet that declares tools with listChanged set to true, and (c) describe the operational problems that occur when the tools capability is omitted (clients unaware of tools or listChanged, missed or stale tool information).","suggested_opener":"During a deployment, clients stop receiving listChanged notifications for tools.","quiz_type_used":"APPLICATION"}

{"authoring_prompt":"Write a brief implementation plan and concise pseudocode for an MCP client that treats the set of tools as dynamic. The client must call tools/list on demand and subscribe to notifications/tools/list_changed to learn about additions, removals, or updates at runtime. Show the exact call sequence you perform immediately before invoking any tool and how list_changed notifications update the client's authoritative view. In one short paragraph, explain how using on-demand listing together with list_changed prevents race conditions.","suggested_opener":"A production agent must call tools/list and subscribe to notifications/tools/list_changed.","quiz_type_used":"IMPLEMENTATION"}

{"authoring_prompt":"Design and implement a UI approval gate that enforces explicit human-in-the-loop approval before any model-invoked tool executes. Define an audit log schema and retention policy that records approvals, invocations, denials, and related metadata for traceability. Provide API contracts and server-side invocation code that require approval tokens and never surface internal errors or diagnostics to clients. Include brief UI mockups, access-control rules, and example sanitization/error-handling snippets.","suggested_opener":"During an integration, model-controlled tools require human-in-the-loop approval in UI.","quiz_type_used":"IMPLEMENTATION"}

{"authoring_prompt":"Provide examinees the quoted line: “Think of MCP like a USB-C port for AI applications…”. Then present a student response that asserts specific protocol mechanics as requirements. Ask candidates to analyze whether the quoted text supports those specific mechanics, identifying each unsupported claim and explaining why. Require a concise model answer and a short rubric that grants full credit only if the respondent concludes the quote is a high-level analogy and cannot by itself justify the listed mechanics.","suggested_opener":"Your team treats MCP like USB-C when connecting AI applications to systems.","quiz_type_used":"ANALYSIS"}

{"authoring_prompt":"Explain why a client API exposes explicit capability flags that are set at construction time, as shown by ClientCapabilities.builder().roots(true).sampling().elicitation(). For each capability—filesystem roots support (with list-change notifications), LLM sampling support, and elicitation capability—analyze plausible implementation trade-offs and operational implications of enabling them. Base your analysis only on the concepts shown in the snippet and give concise, engineer-focused guidance for a design decision.","suggested_opener":"Your team must decide whether to enable roots, sampling, and elicitation.","quiz_type_used":"ANALYSIS"}

{"authoring_prompt":"You are reviewing a transport configured with a custom HttpRequest.Builder that embeds a never-expiring token. Describe the security and operational risks of using a static HttpRequest.Builder and explain why it prevents per-request credential rotation. When dynamic authentication is needed, state the correct approach and name the interfaces to implement. Briefly explain at a high level how implementing McpSyncHttpClientRequestCustomizer or McpAsyncHttpClientRequestCustomizer lets the transport adjust authentication at request time.","suggested_opener":"A production incident shows transport always sends the same never-expiring token.","quiz_type_used":"APPLICATION"}

{"authoring_prompt":"Using the roots capability, describe what breaks when client.addRoot or client.removeRoot is invoked without client.rootsListChangedNotification. Explain how the server's view of accessible filesystem roots becomes stale and why that can lead to incorrect or unsafe behavior. Give two concrete examples of failures or safety issues that could result and state the correct client-side notification sequence.","suggested_opener":"During testing, addRoot and removeRoot calls occur without notification.","quiz_type_used":"APPLICATION"}

{"authoring_prompt":"Describe the failure mode when the wrong HTTP request customizer type is registered for an MCP transport. Be explicit which interfaces the transport expects: McpSyncHttpClientRequestCustomizer or McpAsyncHttpClientRequestCustomizer, and explain why the customizer type must match the MCP client type. State the resulting observable behavior on HTTP request modifications.","suggested_opener":"During a code review you spot McpSyncHttpClientRequestCustomizer used with async MCP client","quiz_type_used":"UNDERSTANDING"}

{"authoring_prompt":"Write a short implementation that ensures the client initializes the connection before calling any APIs. For a sync client show McpClient.sync(transport).build(); call client.initialize(); then call client.listTools(). For an async client describe the async initialize flow you would follow. In 2–4 sentences explain why initialize() is required (mention MCP session, protocol and capability negotiation, and change/notification consumers) and what may fail if it is skipped.","suggested_opener":"During deployment, the McpSyncClient fails to call initialize() before listTools().","quiz_type_used":"IMPLEMENTATION"}
